Answer: A
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification outlining the inferior and anterior border of the cardiac silhouette, which is characteristic of a calcified left ventricular aneurysm. This specific pattern of mural calcification distinguishes it from pericardial calcification (which typically follows the atrioventricular groove or outlines the entire heart) or valvular/annular calcifications.
